title: Metaphor-Induced Cross-Domain Misalignment in Reasoning Models

original_idea.body:
# Metaphor-Induced Cross-Domain Misalignment in Reasoning Models

**Problem:** A 2026 paper (arXiv 2601.03388) reports metaphors are a source of cross-domain misalignment in large reasoning models. This is a fresh, under-replicated angle: framing harmful intent metaphorically may bypass alignment more than literal phrasing.

**Direction:** Using inference only on a small open reasoning model, build matched literal vs metaphorical versions of borderline prompts and compare misalignment/compliance rates, then test whether a few metaphorical in-context examples induce broader misalignment (combining with the in-context EM finding).

**Why it matters:** Maps a non-obvious linguistic attack surface that safety filters trained on literal phrasing miss — a low-compute, training-free red-team direction relevant to robustness of deployed reasoning models.

**Relevant context:** Metaphors are a Source of Cross-Domain Misalignment of Large Reasoning Models (arXiv 2601.03388). In-context EM (arXiv 2510.11288). EM base (arXiv 2502.17424).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain mapping a linguistic attack surface but relies on an under-replicated 2026 claim; gap in catastrophic linkage.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Inference-only on small reasoning model, matched literal/metaphorical prompts; novice-feasible with mentor.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused comparison deliverable, few dependencies, clear success criteria.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Training-free red-team on open models, weak lab incentive; independent-friendly.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference-only, no training; runs on minimal compute.

novelty.reasoning: Based on a fresh 2026 paper; replication/extension angle plausibly open but underexplored.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Based on a fresh 2026 paper; replication/extension angle plausibly open but underexplored.
